question.text: Capstone scenario — Saptarishi Capital Cat II AIF: Commitment INR 400 cr (fully called), tenure 5 yr, Hurdle 8% compounded, Incentive 20% with 100% catch-up, Terminal NAV INR 700 cr. Compute GP CARRY (approx, in INR crore).

explanation.text: The Logic: Total profit = INR 700 - 400 = INR 300 cr. Hurdle NAV Y5 = INR 400 x (1.08)^5 = INR 400 x 1.4693 = INR 587.73 cr, so hurdle return = INR 187.73 cr. Residual above hurdle = INR 300 - 187.73 = INR 112.27 cr. GP target under 100% CATCH-UP = 20% x INR 300 cr = INR 60 crore. Under 100% catch-up, GP receives 100% of residual until it reaches INR 60 cr. Since INR 112.27 cr residual > INR 60 cr, GP fully catches up to INR 60 cr, and balance INR 52.27 cr splits 80/20 with LP getting 80% (INR 41.82 cr) and GP getting 20% (INR 10.45 cr). Wait — that conflicts with '20% of total profit' framing. Re-doing per chapter: '100% catch-up means all residual up to GP's pre-determined share (20% of total profit), then standard sharing thereafter'. So GP catches up to INR 60 cr from residual (consumes INR 60 of INR 112.27 cr), leaving INR 52.27 cr. This INR 52.27 cr is split 80% LP / 20% GP = GP gets another INR 10.45 cr. TOTAL GP carry = INR 60 + INR 10.45 = INR 70.45 cr. However, Chapter 6 Example 6.5(b) interpretation (100% catch-up FULLY absorbs residual to GP until target reached; if residual > target, GP stops at target and all excess goes 80/20) — strictly readings A (INR 60 cr = pure target) is the chapter-aligned answer. The chapter Example 6.5 with 100% catch-up computes GP = total profit x 20% whenever residual >= target — GP target INR 60 cr. The Trap: B is 20% x (300 - 80) confusion; C is no-catch-up carry (20% x 112 = 22 cr app rounding); D is arbitrary. Cross-Exam Context: Chapter 6 Example 6.5(b) interpretation. XIX-C tests same capstone. Manager's Pro-Tip: At large fund sizes, the catch-up + 80/20 residual split creates a non-trivial GP upside on high-performing vintages. Model every vintage scenario for your LP deck — LPs reward GPs who show the math transparently.
